$comment: Per-file, per-rule exceptions for the voice rules in content-lint.mjs. Every entry needs `file` (relative to packages/website; a trailing slash allows a directory), `rule` (a VOICE-* rule id) and a non-empty `reason`. Optional `phrase` narrows the entry to one phrase id from the rule tables. An entry without a reason fails the lint.

entries.reason: The chapter quotes a customer reply the model drafts. Sie is the correct form in German business correspondence, so the example keeps it while the chapter around it stays Du.
A glossary example quotes a formal notice addressed to a third party, where Sie is correct; the surrounding reference text stays Du.
The chapter teaches readers to recognise filler in their own prompts, so the banned words appear inside quoted bad examples, two of them within frozen code fences.
The announcing openers are quoted weak prompts the chapter then rewrites; removing them would delete the lesson.
Quoted boilerplate of a bad acquisition mail addressed to a client, where German business correspondence uses Sie.
Quoted speech addressed to the reader client, where Sie is the correct German form.
Quoted client question in a sales scene, where Sie is the correct German form.

"Robustness" is the statutory term in the Article 15 heading of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 ("accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity"). The lesson on human oversight names it once in its key concepts and once when quoting Article 15(1); a synonym would misname the requirement, and the German twin cites the same term as "Robustheit".

"Umfassend" is the scoping qualifier the primacy claim in the KI-Verordnung entry rests on, matching the Commission own wording "the first-ever comprehensive legal framework on AI worldwide". Without it the entry asserts that no AI-specific legal framework existed anywhere before 1 August 2024, which AI rules already in force elsewhere contradict. Load-bearing legal qualifier, not an intensifier.

English twin of the German KI-Verordnung entry. "Comprehensive" carries the same scoping the primacy claim depends on and mirrors the Commission own wording; dropping it in one locale alone would also break the bilingual pair.
